name: Pierpont prime criterion for neusis-constructible n-gons

knowledge.progressSummary: COMPLETE: AngleTrisectionOQ04OQ03.lean compiles with 0 sorries, 0 axioms
insights: Pierpont primes p are those where p-1 = 2^u * 3^v; this is the key criterion for neusis constructibility
Nat.add_sub_cancel in Mathlib v4.26 takes EXPLICIT arguments n and m, not implicit
norm_num handles Nat.Prime for large primes (73, 97, 109, 193) where by decide hits max recursion depth
native_decide efficiently computes Nat.totient for specific values
interval_cases p works elegantly when bounds p ≤ 3 and 2 ≤ p are established to enumerate p ∈ {2, 3}
builtItems: Is23Smooth: 3-smooth positive integers (prime factors only 2 and 3)
IsPierpontPrime: prime p such that p-1 is 3-smooth
prime_factor_not_two_three_of_smooth: key private helper using Nat.le_of_dvd + interval_cases
fermatPrime_is_pierpont: Fermat primes are Pierpont primes
Totient computations via native_decide + IsTwoThreeNumber proofs for 7, 9, 13, 19, 37
Non-constructibility for 11-gon and 23-gon proved via prime factor obstruction
mathlibGaps: Full Galois-theoretic proof of neusis constructibility iff phi(n) is 2-3-smooth is not in Mathlib
No Mathlib lemma for 'Pierpont prime' as a named concept
nextSteps: OQ-04-OQ-04: Could formalize the converse direction - if phi(n) is NOT 2-3-smooth then n-gon is NOT neusis-constructible
